newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent up, looking to test resistance.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent up, looking to test resistance.

text.p: Brent crude futures prices were firmer in late trading on Wednesday supported by short covering after the failure to break $22.50 earlier this week.
Brokers said API data overnight from the U.S. was having a limited affect on the market, although heating oil was given a boost.
March Brent on SIMEX was last traded at $22.34 per barrel, up nine cents from London's settlement of $22.25.
One broker said he was targeting a break of resistance at $22.44 -- the intraday high on Monday when prices tested $22.00.

API data showed crude stocks rose 3.73 million barrels, compared with expectations averaging 3.00 million barrels. Distillates fell 2.85 million, versus expectations of 2.00 million and gasoline rose 1.84 million against expectations at 2.25 million.
Brokers said the gain in crude data was shrugged off, but the draw on heating oil offered some support.

NYMEX March crude futures on ACCESS were last traded at an intraday high of $24.07, up 17, while heating oil was up 0.57 cent at 67.40 cents per gallon but had not traded for several hours. -- Singapore Newsroom (+65-870 3081)
